newsitem.title: INDIA: Speculative purchases lift Delhi shares.
newsitem.headline: Speculative purchases lift Delhi shares.

text.p: Selective buying by domestic financial institutions and speculators pushed up Delhi share prices in afternoon trade at the start of a settlement period, brokers said on Monday.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index was 5.55 points higher at 862.77 points at 12.45 p.m. (0715 GMT).
"Buying activity was mainly of a speculative nature which helped lift share prices," said Bharat Bhushan Aggarwal of brokers Nu-Era Equities.
Brokers said shares of Reliance Industries and Smithkline Beecham Consumer Healthcare Ltd were in spotlight.
Reliance Industries rose 5.10 rupees to 345.70 on speculative purchases, brokers said.

Smithkline Beecham shot up 17.00 rupees to 338.00 rupees on strong buying by foreign institutional investors following the announcement of better-than-expected half- yearly results by the company, brokers said.
The company on Thursday announced a 19.3 percent increase in its net profit for the six months that ended on June 30.
State Bank of India quoted 1.00 rupee higher at 329.00.
Larsen and Toubro gained 5.75 rupees to 253.75.
